briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Anthropic Claude 4.5 escalate frontier race as US export curbs tighten on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race intensified this week with multiple frontier model releases and record infrastructure spending. US-China chip restrictions are reshaping global compute access while safety concerns mount over agentic systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with advanced multi-agent capabilities; Anthropic launched Claude 4.5 focusing on long-horizon tasks; Google DeepMind previewed Gemini 3; Meta open-sourced Llama 4 400B; xAI deployed Grok-3; DeepSeek unveiled R2. Reasoning benchmarks show 18% gains across leading labs.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New EU AI Act enforcement guidelines target agent autonomy risks.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA announced Blackwell Ultra clusters shipping to Microsoft and xAI; TSMC broke ground on three new Arizona fabs; Saudi Arabia committed $40B to sovereign AI data centers; power constraints delay 25% of planned 2026 deployments.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent coordination protocols outpace safety alignment by 2027?
